findings.claim: This hadith text is the named source your exam expects you to cite for the Five Pillars of belief.
findings.truth: Kitab al-iman 1:4 is the source for the SIX Beliefs. The Five Pillars are practices (Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm, Hajj), not beliefs, and the same Key Fact box lists six items immediately above.

findings.claim: The Qur'an states He is “closer to you than your jugular vein” (Surah 50:16).
findings.truth: No published translation uses the second person here. Khattab: 'We are closer to them than their jugular vein'; Saheeh International: 'closer to him than [his] jugular vein'.
findings.evidence: quran.com/50/16 (Khattab, The Clear Quran)

findings.claim: 'Describe what Muslims believe about the nature of Allah.' typed '3 marks — Describe'

Saheeh International: 'Say, He is Allah, [who is] One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge.' Surah 112 is named in the spec and students memorise this wording for the fifth mark.

findings.claim: all pilgrims wear identical white garments (ihram)

findings.claim: The Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam (Wajibat) include the Five Pillars (Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Hajj, and Shahadah through Walayah) plus additional obligations: Khums, Jihad, commanding good, forbidding evil, and love/disavowal (Tawallah and Tabarra).
findings.truth: The Ten Obligatory Acts (Furu ad-Din) are Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Khums, Hajj, Jihad, Amr-bil-Maroof, Nahy-anil-Munkar, Tawallah and Tabarra. Shahadah is not one of them and 'Walayah' does not appear in the list. As written the sentence also totals eleven items, so it cannot be the Ten. The lesson's own main paragraph gets this right, so the collapsible contradicts it.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1 (Ten Obligatory Acts, links with the Five Pillars); lesson L4 paragraph n16

findings.claim: the Sunni-Shi'a difference on Salah (three times vs five) ... The most common failure is a Discuss answer that treats “another point of view” as a single brief sentence.
findings.truth: Shi'a Muslims pray the same five prayers, combined into three prayer times; 'three times vs five' reads as three prayers. Plus the Discuss / Evaluate error and an unevidenced examiner claim. The lesson body already states the correct position.

findings.claim: Model answer on greater jihad: 'Surah 22:39 describes the striving of those who have been wronged, but the broader context of the surah is that striving for God encompasses all dimensions of life' and then 'The named source — Surah 2:190-194 constrains lesser jihad'.
findings.truth: Surah 22:39 is permission to fight for those who have been attacked, and Surah 2:190-194 sets the conditions on lesser jihad. Neither supports greater jihad. Surah 29:69 ('those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways') is a correct anchor for striving.

findings.claim: Surah 53 (An-Najm, The Star) — the surah in which the Prophet Muhammad's Night Journey (Isra) and his receiving of divine revelation are described.
findings.truth: The Night Journey (Isra) is Surah 17:1. Surah 53 describes the revelation and the Prophet's vision at the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary (53:13-18), which tradition links to the ascension, not the Isra.

findings.claim: Sunni “around 85% of Muslims worldwide”; Shi'a “around 15%”.
findings.truth: Pew Research puts Sunni Muslims at 87-90% and Shi'a at 10-13%. 85/15 sits just outside the usual range but is a common textbook simplification and costs no marks.
findings.evidence: Pew Research Center, Mapping the Global Muslim Population (2009)

findings.claim: Several Qur'an quotations are hybrids of two published translations rather than verbatim from one: Surah 2:136 and 32:11 (L2), 2:190 and 22:39 (L5), 53:4, 4:115 and 2:271 (L6), 16:36 (L1).
findings.truth: Each is semantically faithful and close to a published wording (Yusuf Ali, Saheeh International, Khattab or Abdel Haleem), so none changes the meaning or the mark. Recorded rather than edited: re-quoting all of them would touch narration in seven places for no gain in accuracy. The two that were NOT faithful (Surah 112, Surah 50:16) are fixed as F5b and F2.
findings.evidence: quran.com; Wikipedia translation tables

findings.claim: This lesson covers 16 spec points in two sections.
findings.truth: Sections 3 and 4 do contain 16 points, but the lesson does not teach all of them: 4.4 (Shi'a obligatory actions), 4.5-4.6 (Sufi fasting, the Sheikh) are thin and 4.7 (dance, music and poetry, including the divergent views on music) is absent. A coverage gap, not a wrong statement, so it is recorded for the content owner rather than edited.
findings.evidence: spec 1C sections 3 and 4 vs raw/L06.txt

findings.claim: Khums is described only as '20% of surplus income' paid to 'the Imam's representatives (the religious scholars)'.
findings.truth: ADJUDICATE: in Twelver practice khums is split into two halves, sahm al-Imam (paid through the marja) and sahm al-sada (paid to descendants of the Prophet). The spec asks only for the nature, role and significance of khums, so the simplification is defensible for GCSE. Recommendation: leave as is unless Tom wants the two-share detail added.
findings.evidence: spec 2.5; standard Twelver jurisprudence
findings.ruling: Leave: stem widening / khums split beyond spec scope (relabel queue).

summary: Doctrine and scripture are mostly sound, but the whole unit was written to the wrong question paper: every lesson carries a 3-mark 'Describe' question (this paper has no Describe question and the spec sets Describe at 4 marks) and a 12-mark 'Discuss' question (the command word is Evaluate), each with an invented band ladder. Three HIGH content errors: Kitab al-iman 1:4 credited with the Five Pillars instead of the Six Beliefs, an invented rendering of Surah 112, and a Ten Obligatory Acts list that includes Shahadah and totals eleven items.
